Power-Law Head of a Compiled CDF Derivative

Source: R/cdf_compiled.R
compiled_cdf_head.Rd

The part of \(\partial_I F(q) = \int_0^q f B_I\) below the cut \(y_0\) that cdf_rule_cpp() reports for a family on \((0, \infty)\) whose density behaves like \(y^{\alpha - 1}\) near zero (a gamma or a generalized gamma with a small shape), where part of the mass lies below the smallest representable double.

Usage

compiled_cdf_head(distrib, rule, th, order, params)

Arguments

distrib

A family named in compiled_cdf_deriv_k().

rule

The list cdf_rule_cpp() returns.

th

The named list of parameter vectors, one value per point.

order

The derivative order, 3 or 4.

params

The parameter names.

Value

NULL when no point has a head; otherwise a list with idx, the points that have one, and integral, a function of a multi-index that returns the head's integral at those points.

Details

On \((0, y_0]\), with \(L = \log y\), every derivative of \(\ell\) in the parameters is linear in \(L\), so it is read at \(10^{-290}\) and 15 units of \(L\) below it and extended to any \(L\); \(B_I\) is then a polynomial in \(L\) of degree at most four, and $$\int_{-\infty}^{L_0} e^{c + \alpha u} B_I(u)\, du = \frac{f(y_0)\, y_0}{\alpha} \int_0^\infty e^{-t} B_I(L_0 - t/\alpha)\, dt$$ is taken by the three-point Gauss-Laguerre rule, exact for a polynomial of degree five. The cut, \(\alpha\) and \(f(y_0)\,y_0\) come from cdf_rule_cpp(), which uses the same head at orders one and two.
